description: Definition values recovered from the source papers for records whose table or figure does not state them. Applied by scripts/annotate-definitions.mjs only where the record's value is undocumented; a stated value is never overwritten (the script fails on a conflict). Every fill cites the arXiv source, the section, a short quote and the SHA-256 of the arXiv source archive read.

evidence.citation: Katz et al. 2023, SPHINX-20 data release (arXiv:2309.03269)
evidence.where: Sec. 4 Discussion, subsection 'Caveats' (list of modelling assumptions of SPHINX)
evidence.quote: For example, we have chosen a specific stellar IMF (Kroupa-like), a stellar population synthesis library ({\small BPASS}) for the stellar spectra
evidence.note: The paper says 'Kroupa-like' and gives a high-mass slope of -1.35 with a 100 Msun upper limit; Kroupa (2001) is the nearest entry in this dataset's vocabulary. It is a simulation-wide assumption stated in the caveats.

set.gasStatistic: median of the gas fractions above a threshold (galaxies below it are counted separately)

evidence.where: Sec. 4.3 'Gas Fractions' (text before Fig. fraction)
evidence.quote: we now count the fraction of galaxies that lie below the threshold, $f_{\rm low}$, and compute the median and 68\% scatter of those gas fractions that lie above the threshold.
evidence.note: The paper says plain means or medians over all galaxies are not appropriate for these fractions.

set.gasMethod: centre of the shaded region spanned by nine HI/H2 partition methods (no single model)

evidence.where: Sec. 3.2 'Modelling the HI/H2 Fractions'
evidence.quote: Thus, the \hi and \htwo masses of each galaxy are estimated by a total of nine different methods. In the forthcoming figures, we shade the region between the models but do not show the individual models to avoid crowding.
evidence.note: The paper is agnostic about which of the nine methods is best and shades the region between them; the stored record's own warning says the plotted median is the centre of the dark band.

evidence.where: Sec. 7.1.1 'The galaxy stellar mass function', paragraph after Fig. smhm (stellar-to-halo mass ratio)
evidence.quote: we define the halo mass as the mass within the radius for which the mean internal density is equal to the critical overdensity provided by \citet{Bryan1998}
evidence.note: Halo mass is the Bryan & Norman (1998) virial mass, not M200c; the paper contrasts its use of the current halo mass with the peak halo mass of Behroozi+19 (main.tex line 1060, same paragraph).

evidence.citation: SWIFT/VELOCIraptor comparison-data compilation, conversion script for Kirby et al. 2013
evidence.where: comment string written into the converted file
evidence.quote: There is also a correction of {kroupa_to_chabrier_mass} on the stellar masses to convert from Kroupa to the Chabrier IMF.
evidence.note: The paper's masses assume a Kroupa IMF; the compilation multiplies them by 0.912 (Kroupa to Chabrier), so the stored masses are on a Chabrier IMF. This is the compilation's statement, not the paper's. The sha256 is that of the conversion script, not an arXiv archive.

readWithoutResult.note: Chabrier IMF is stated for the SPS photometry and for the observations compared with, not for the simulation stellar mass; no aperture stated. The SFR averaging timescale, the epoch of the halo mass and the black hole mass method are not stated for the tables. Read a second time on 2026-10-18. Chabrier is named only for the SED library and for observations converted to it; no stellar-mass, SFR-timescale, halo-mass-epoch or black-hole-mass definition is given for the simulation tables.

The source text has no statement of the stellar-mass definition behind the plotted mass function. The cosmic star formation history is shown without a statement of how it was integrated or of the SFR indicator. Read a second time on 2026-10-18. The stellar mass of a galaxy is not defined; the star formation history figure caption states none of the four SFR-density keys; the paper has no black hole mass versus stellar mass figure.

Uses total stellar mass of each simulation, and states the computations may differ between simulations; no per-simulation aperture or IMF. Read a second time on 2026-10-18. The paper says the stellar masses are 'total' and may be computed differently in each simulation, and names no IMF; an aperture given in an appendix applies only to eight matched galaxies.
No stellar-mass aperture stated for the main-sequence figures. Read a second time on 2026-10-18. The stellar mass behind the main-sequence figures is not defined.

No radius restriction for j; stellar-mass definition not stated. Read a second time on 2026-10-18. The stellar mass is not defined; j is defined for all stellar particles of the subhalo without a radius cut.

Stellar-mass definition for sizes and black-hole relations not stated in the sections searched. The zoom volume is given in Mpc without saying comoving or physical. Read a second time on 2026-10-18. Stated only for the stellar mass density and for one selection-corrected mass function curve; not stated for the size and black hole relations or for the density frame (the volume is the initial (16 Mpc)^3).

SFR is stars formed in the last 200 Myr within 0.2 R_vir; the stellar-mass definition is not restated. Read a second time on 2026-10-18. Only the SFR is defined (star particles within 0.2 R_vir formed in the last 200 Myr).

Comoving versus physical density is not stated for the mass function. Read a second time on 2026-10-18. No statement of comoving or physical for the mass function or the star formation rate density; comoving appears only for box length and softening.
IMF of the simulation stellar populations not stated in the data-release paper.
j measured within r50 or 5 r50; stellar-mass definition not restated.

The stellar mass function, size, SFMS and angular-momentum sections do not state which of the paper's mass apertures the released tables use. Read a second time on 2026-10-18. The mass function, size and main-sequence figures do not state the stellar-mass aperture; the paper states M*_{R_0.1} for the angular-momentum, mass-metallicity and other figures only, and it is not carried over by inference.

Not stated for the TNG records and for the EAGLE mass function and sSFR records. The TNG IMF is not stated either. Read a second time on 2026-10-18. No IMF for IllustrisTNG; no density frame for any of the three; no SFR timescale for EAGLE or IllustrisTNG, and for SIMBA only the per-element law is given.
The stellar-to-halo mass figure does not state the halo mass definition in the caption or nearby text.

Not stated for the SIMBA and FIREbox comparison curves. Read on 2026-10-18. The SIMBA and FIREbox mass-metallicity curves are adopted from Garcia et al. 2025 and Feldmann et al. 2023 and the stellar-mass definition is not restated; the 3 kpc aperture given is for the oxygen abundance.

Comoving versus physical density of the mass function is not stated. Read a second time on 2026-10-18. The box volume is given as (15 cMpc/h)^3 and the mass function is built from 1/V weights, but no sentence says the density is per comoving volume; not inferred.

FOF and SUBFIND stellar masses are both shown; which one the digitized relations use is not stated. Read a second time on 2026-10-18. Star particles are attached to the host FOF halo and the stellar mass function text says 'stars within FOF halos', but no sentence ties the stellar-to-halo mass or metallicity figures to a mass definition; not inferred.

Read again on 2026-10-18. The cosmic star formation rate density panel (Fig. 4, top left) is plotted without saying how it was computed; the only use of 'instantaneous' is for the local star formation rate that drives the wind model, not for the plotted curve.

Read on 2026-10-18. The paper mentions the initial mass function only in general terms and defers the model to the NIHAO base paper; the base paper (Wang et al. 2015, arXiv:1503.04818) states a Milky Way-type IMF only for the abundance-matching comparison, not for the simulation's stellar particles.
Read on 2026-10-18. The stellar-to-halo mass figure and its text do not state which halo mass is used or at what epoch.

Read on 2026-10-18. The data-release paper describes the group catalogues but does not state the halo mass used in the released stellar-to-halo mass table (smhm_Thesan1.dat), whose header gives only the column names.
